verdict.rationale: Stripe's public pricing page lists the flat processing rates that agent-driven orders appear to inherit (2.9% + 30¢ domestic, plus published adders for international cards and currency conversion), and machine-payment minimums are documented per rail. That lets a merchant estimate base processing cost without contacting sales. However, the evidence never states an agentic-channel fee schedule, or explicitly confirms that ACS adds no surcharge. The only reference to agent-platform economics is an unquantified "small fee on completed purchases" that merchants pay, so the full cost of an agentic channel cannot be priced from published material. Missing for 10: an explicit published ACS/agentic fee schedule (or a stated zero surcharge), quantified agent-platform fees, and stablecoin/SPT rail fee rates.
